headlines.title: McDonald's is leaning into chicken and drinks to grow. New data shows it could be a tough task
headlines.summary: McDonald's is targeting growth in chicken and beverages, but Consumer Edge data shows Chick-fil-A and coffee chains gaining in customer spending.
headlines.article_text: McDonald's chicken and beverage growth faces rivals Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points McDonald's is pegging its growth hopes on chicken and beverages, but data shows it is losing spending share to key rivals like Chick-fil-A. Coffee chains like Dutch Bros. and Starbucks are also gaining ground, according to Consumer Edge. McDonald's growth plan includes rolling out hand-breaded chicken items and bringing grilled chicken back to its menu. In this article MCD Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A chicken sandwich from McDonald's is shown in Chicago, Illinois, May 6, 2021. Scott Olson | Getty Images McDonald's is betting on chicken and beverages to fuel its next phase of growth, but new consumer spending data suggests the fast-food giant faces stiff competition from rivals that specialize in those areas. At its September investor day, McDonald's outlined plans to gain an additional 1.5 percentage points of global market share in both chicken and beverages by 2030. The chain identified the categories as significant opportunities to expand its business beyond beef. CEO Chris Kempczinski told CNBC the size of those markets underscores the potential upside. "Chicken is a $130 billion category. We have about a 20% share of chicken. Beverages is about a $230 billion category. We have a 10% share of beverages," Kempczinski said, saying McDonald's has more room to grow in those areas than in the $50 billion global beef category, where it has about a 40% share. But new data indicates McDonald's could have a tough task in gaining spending from chicken and drink rivals. Many of the restaurant chains winning the most spending from McDonald's diners specialize in those two segments, according to exclusive data shared by Consumer Edge, which tracks credit and debit card transactions. Among McDonald's customers, Chick-fil-A gained 0.58 percentage points of limited-service restaurant spending in the third quarter compared with a year earlier, making it the biggest gainer among the chains tracked by Consumer Edge. Coffee businesses are also capturing more spending from McDonald's customers. Drive-thru-only chain 7 Brew added 0.4 percentage points, while Starbucks , Dutch Bros. Coffee and Dunkin' also ranked among the top 10 gainers. Together, the four coffee chains added 0.88 percentage points of spending share. McDonald's remained by far the largest individual chain in customers' overall limited-service restaurant spending, but its share declined from a year earlier. Restaurant Brands International -owned Burger King, meanwhile, gained 0.24 percentage points, the largest increase among burger chains. "There’s a big battle for a smaller amount of restaurant spend as people become more selective in what they spend," said Michael Gunther, Consumer Edge senior vice president. The data says only so much about the competitive landscape for McDonald's in the chicken and drink spaces, in part because they don't track exactly what customers are ordering at the counter. "If they [McDonald's] are able to attract diners with interesting options, it could work,” Gunther added. While McDonald's has struggled with sluggish sales, executives have said they saw signs of improvement toward the end of the third quarter. At its investor day, McDonald's said U.S. comparable sales were slightly negative in July and August, but the company said it expected September to turn positive. Consumer Edge data similarly showed McDonald's year-over-year spending share declines narrowing across every income group in September. Wall Street has also questioned how quickly the chicken and beverage strategy can deliver. Bernstein analyst Danilo Gargiulo said after McDonald's investor day that U.S. beverage launches had not generated enough sales to offset broader weakness, while the company's next chicken platform — which includes hand-breaded chicken and grilled chicken menu items — was further away than he expected. "The scale of investment required to deliver [the company's growth plan] McDonald's Next was above our expectations and introduces additional pressure on near-term earnings," said Gargiulo in his note. He has a market perform rating on the stock and $295 price target. Shares closed around $235 on Friday. headlines.article_text: Microsoft will mainly use its Maia chips for AI inference Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Microsoft said it will eventually have multiple gigawatts worth of its Maia AI chips. The company intends to make Maia its primary architecture for running AI models. The next-generation Maia 300 chip enters production in 2027. In this article MSFT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT A Microsoft Azure Maia 300 prototype chip. Microsoft Microsoft will ramp up use of its homegrown artificial intelligence chips after years of reliance on Nvidia's graphics processing units, as the software giant attempts to bolster its AI stack. Starting with its third-generation Maia AI accelerator, unveiled on Monday, Microsoft said it will mainly rely on its own silicon to handle incoming requests. Microsoft's greatest strength in AI has been its Azure cloud, which runs a series of models for clients. Its Microsoft 365 Copilot and GitHub Copilot offer AI-powered services to software engineers and other office workers. And the company develops in-house models, though they've yet to make a big splash in a market dominated by OpenAI , Anthropic and Google . The emerging opportunity in chips stems from unrelenting demand for advanced processors and a desire in the market for choice. Nvidia's GPUs have been the standard for AI workloads and models, and they fill Microsoft's existing data centers, while also serving to train models from OpenAI and Anthropic. But as demand keeps growing, the model leaders have embraced a variety of silicon from companies including Amazon , Advanced Micro Devices , Cerebras , Google and, in recent months, Microsoft. For general-purpose use, Microsoft already taps its own central processing units as well as silicon from Intel and AMD . Finance chief Amy Hood said at a Goldman Sachs conference last month that use of its own chips has helped with "margin improvement over the course of a decade." Microsoft introduced its inaugural AI chip, the Maia 100, in 2023 . It touted the Maia 200 this past January , and CEO Satya Nadella told analysts in July that Maia 200 "delivers 30% better performance per dollar than the latest generation hardware in our fleet" and said it was handling OpenAI models. Production of the Maia 300 starts in 2027. Microsoft is targeting multi-gigawatt deployments of chips in the Maia family, according to a blog post from Executive Vice President Scott Guthrie. But Alistair Speirs, a general manager, declined to provide a timeline. "We reserve a little bit of optionality there, because this is an industry that's changing very fast, and we want to deploy the right silicon for the right models that we're using at the right time as well," Speirs said. Read more CNBC tech news AI's quiet safety gatekeepers are stepping into the spotlight Microsoft's Nadella says AI needs an 'emergency brake' that humans control Nvidia GPUs are everywhere. Here are the ways companies are accessing them Hollywood takes on Zuckerberg, Musk and Altman amid widespread anxiety over AI Microsoft expects to pack 96 Maia 300 chips into each data center rack, double the number for the Maia 200. The new version can run through up to seven times more AI tokens per rack, with 40% more tokens per megawatt when compared with GPUs. "We need new architectures that will give us essentially better performance, better use of the power that we have," Speirs said. "You can think of power translating pretty directly into operational cost for something like a data center as well." Parts of Microsoft 365 Copilot should speed up with Maia 300, said Jim Kleewein, a technical fellow at the company. In a note distributed to clients on Wednesday, Evercore ISI analysts estimated that Maia will represent about 10% of Microsoft's spending on AI chips by the first quarter of 2027. The analysts recommend buying Microsoft shares. Nvidia will still be a big part of the equation. CEO Jensen Huang spoke at an event last week where Microsoft announced a Surface laptop containing an Nvidia processor. And when it comes to training models, Microsoft partners with Nvidia and AMD, Speirs said. Unlike Google's tensor processing units or Amazon's Inferentia and Trainium, Microsoft's accelerators can't be rented by the hour to other companies. "Nobody has tested them outside of Microsoft yet," said Patrick Moorhead, CEO of advisory firm Moor Insights and Strategy.
